note: Thanksgiving edition: lighter newsletter volume, so a shorter list today.

top.title: Anthropic: companies get the most from AI by reorganizing work, not cutting staff
top.summary: Anthropic interviewed 58 US enterprise customers about roughly 300 AI use cases. The biggest gains came from reshaping roles and task ownership around the models, while the main blockers were employee resistance and steps AI hasn't sped up yet, like review and decision-making.
top.why: Gives you evidence for an enablement pitch built on redesigning PMM roles and handoffs, and flags review as the bottleneck to design your workflows around.

top.title: Claude now picks up skills delivered by MCP servers
top.summary: With Skills over MCP, a connected app can hand Claude its own how-to instructions with no separate install. It is in public beta and on by default for Pro, Max and Ultra plans.
top.why: You could ship PMM skills alongside an MCP connector so every teammate gets the same, versioned instructions instead of copying skill files around.

top.title: OpenAI pilots Private Inference so it can't see enterprise query data
top.summary: OpenAI is piloting a mode that runs a company's queries on its top models without OpenAI being able to see the data, starting with a first group of enterprise customers.
top.why: Raises the bar for what Legal and Security can ask of every vendor, including Anthropic, when you propose sending customer or deal data through marketing workflows.

try_this.title: Make every workflow change prove itself before you keep it
try_this.how: Borrow the loop from this Claude Code skill: before editing a PMM skill or prompt, fix a small test set, a quality check and a budget, state what the change should improve, then keep it only if the scored output actually gets better. Revert anything that doesn't.

workflows.title: MKT1: 30 things marketers can build with AI skills and agents
workflows.summary: A long guide that pushes marketers from prompting to building: brand voice checkers, customer benchmark tools and reusable skills, connected to Claude and ChatGPT through MCP.
workflows.why: A ready-made idea backlog to compare against your PMM workflow roadmap and intake requests.

workflows.title: A Claude Code workflow where automated checks decide what ships
workflows.summary: A reader built a pipeline where Claude writes a brief, Claude Code builds from it, and accessibility checks block any output that fails, with no manual override. The failure report goes back to Claude to fix and resubmit.
workflows.why: The same gate pattern works for PMM content: run brand, claims and terminology checks automatically before a human ever reviews.

workflows.title: Cloudflare lets AI agents search a site and get Markdown back
workflows.summary: Search for Agents adds a search endpoint to a site so agents can query it and receive Markdown results. It is a beta toggle in the Cloudflare dashboard.
workflows.why: Worth raising with web and docs owners: agent-readable docs and product pages affect how coding agents describe Camunda to developers.

governance.title: Amazon: attackers' AI agents found and exploited a zero-day with almost no human input
governance.summary: Agents running an open-source pen-testing framework found and exploited a flaw from a single goal prompt, and Palo Alto Networks tracked a related campaign that breached at least 10 organizations.
governance.why: Expect Security to tighten review of any agent or connector with write access; build your workflows with scoped permissions and logs from the start.

governance.title: Startups pitch encryption to keep employee prompts away from model makers
governance.summary: TrustedRouter offers end-to-end encryption of employee AI prompts, aimed at companies that don't want model providers seeing their questions.
governance.why: Another sign that prompt privacy is becoming a standard procurement question for any AI tool your team adopts.

measurement.title: Scrunch lifted its AI answer mention rate from 15% to 40% in two months
measurement.summary: Scrunch's playbook: refresh existing content, earn placements on trusted third-party sites and publish targeted FAQs. It also found AI citations decay within six to eight weeks without updates.
measurement.why: AI mention rate is a measurable KPI for Camunda's category story, and the decay window suggests a refresh cadence for a monitoring workflow.

landscape.title: OpenAI merges Chat and Work usage limits and retires GPT-5.6 on Dec. 23
landscape.summary: Chat and Work will share one usage meter, so heavy users may hit limits sooner as the rollout widens in December. Separately, GPT-5.6 and its Sol and Terra variants leave Chat, Work and Codex on Dec. 23.
landscape.why: Check any ChatGPT-based team workflows pinned to GPT-5.6 and retest them on the replacement model before the cutoff.
